name: Local AI Server
author: SYJohnm
description: Run a local llama.cpp or ollama server from the bar: any llama.cpp build or fork (picked per model), live prompt/generation speed, per-model tuning, and the prompt cache kept across restarts. Direct llama-server, or native router mode serving every model from one process. Several instances at once, plus a System One decision model alongside them on its own build.

barWidget.description: Run a local llama.cpp or ollama server from the bar: any llama.cpp build or fork (picked per model), live prompt/generation speed, per-model tuning, and the prompt cache kept across restarts. Direct llama-server, or native router mode serving every model from one process. Several instances at once, plus a System One decision model alongside them on its own build.

schema.label: Backend
schema.description: Which chat server to manage. Can also be switched from the panel. A System One decision model runs alongside it, on its own port and its own build, and is turned on from the Server page.

options.label: ollama
options.description: ollama serve; throughput per completed request

schema.label: Preferred llama-server binary
schema.description: Optional. Every llama.cpp build on the machine is detected (upstream, distro package, forks under ~); this one is preferred when a model is on Auto.

schema.label: Extra llama-server binary
schema.description: Optional. A build the scan does not find on its own (installed somewhere unusual). It joins the Build list on the Model tab.

schema.label: Models directory
schema.description: Leave blank to auto-detect (~/models, ~/.cache/llama.cpp, LM Studio, jan).

schema.label: System One binary
schema.description: Binary override for the decision model. Normally left blank: its build is picked on the Server page, which is the point of running it alongside an older chat fork.

schema.label: System One models directory
schema.description: Where the decision models live. Leave blank to use the main model scan.

schema.label: Server instances
schema.description: How many persistent llama-server instances to manage. Each one gets its own port (host:port and the ports above it), model and build, and can be started or unloaded on its own from the Server page. llama.cpp only, and a single instance in router mode, where one process already serves every model.
